# **Technical Documentation and Subsystem Analysis of the CynageOS Shell Architecture**

The CynageOS desktop shell suite represents a modular, event-driven user interface ecosystem designed specifically for the Niri scrollable-tiling Wayland compositor1. Built using GTK4, gtk4-layer-shell, Tokio asynchronous runtimes, DBus abstractions, and native PulseAudio bindings, the suite provides desktop UI capabilities including an animated application dock, a system control center overlay, a dynamic status bar with an integrated clipboard collector, an asynchronous DBus notification server, an On-Screen Display (OSD) hardware feedback overlay, and server-side window decorations1.  
This documentation provides an exhaustive, statement-by-statement and block-by-block technical breakdown of the six core Rust modules that compose the CynageOS shell ecosystem: altdock.rs, ctrl.rs, main.rs, notifications.rs, osd.rs, and ssd.rs1.

## **Subsystem Architectural Overview**

The architecture decouples hardware event loops, compositor Inter-Process Communication (IPC), and user interface rendering into isolated thread contexts1. The user interface relies on GTK4 bindings paired with gtk4-layer-shell to anchor overlay surfaces to specific Wayland layer surfaces (Layer::Top, Layer::Overlay, Layer::Bottom)1. Cross-thread communication uses Multi-Producer, Single-Consumer (std::sync::mpsc) channels and Tokio asynchronous channels, ensuring that the main GTK event loop remains unblocked during synchronous IO operations, network socket reads, sysfs polling, and IPC socket streaming1.  
The table below outlines the primary responsibilities, execution contexts, layer shell surface anchors, and external IPC interfaces across all six subsystem modules.

| Module | Core Responsibility | Threading and Async Execution Model | External Protocol and System Interfaces | GTK4 / Layer Shell Surface Configuration |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| altdock.rs | Application dock UI, window switcher, hover previews, and cubic easing displacement animations1. | Background event loop thread with ![][image1] local timer ticks1. | Niri IPC Unix Socket (niri msg \-j event-stream, focus-window, MoveFloatingWindow)1. | ApplicationWindow (Layer::Top, Edge::Top)1. |
| ctrl.rs | System control panel, Cairo circular avatar renderer, Wi-Fi access point scanner, sound sink viewer3. | Dedicated MPSC watcher threads polling sysfs and CLI processes3. | Linux Kernel /sys/class/net, /sys/class/rfkill, wpctl, pactl, nmcli, iw3. | ApplicationWindow (Layer::Top, full-screen backdrop overlay)3. |
| main.rs | Shell orchestrator, top bar, drag-and-drop clipboard collector (clippy), probe config parser, workspace state toggler2. | Probe watcher thread, UNIX signal listeners (SIGUSR1), GLib timeouts2. | /var/lib/cynager/info.probe, Niri IPC Socket (Request::Windows, Request::FocusedOutput)2. | TimeCapsule (Layer::Top), Notification Panel (Layer::Bottom), OSD (Layer::Overlay)2. |
| notifications.rs | Async DBus notification daemon, notification sound engine, expandable status bar notification popups4. | Tokio async runtime thread hosting DBus server alongside GTK main context local task4. | DBus Session Bus (org.freedesktop.Notifications), rodio audio output stream4. | Integrated within main.rs TimeCapsule and capsuleN surfaces2. |
| osd.rs | Hardware feedback overlays for volume adjustment, microphone mute state, and screen brightness5. | Native PulseAudio C-mainloop integration (libpulse-glib) with Linux inotify watcher5. | PulseAudio Introspection API (@DEFAULT\_SINK@, @DEFAULT\_SOURCE@), /sys/class/backlight5. | ApplicationWindow (Layer::Overlay, Edge::Bottom)5. |
| ssd.rs | Server-Side Window Decorations tracking focused tiling and floating window boundaries6. | Threaded Niri IPC event loop coupled with ![][image1] (![][image2]) GTK geometry tracking loop6. | Niri IPC Socket (Request::EventStream, Request::FocusedWindow), ydotool key synthesis6. | ApplicationWindow (Layer::Overlay, Edge::Top/Left)6. |

## **Chapter 1: Architectural Analysis of altdock.rs**

The altdock.rs module implements the dock interface1. It handles application icon rendering, active focus indicators, hover previews, and animated window nudging mechanics interacting directly with Niri's floating window manager1.

### **Data Structures and Serialization Primitives**

The module defines the NiriWindow structure to hold window state1:

```Rust  
\#\[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)\]  
pub struct NiriWindow {  
    pub id: u64,  
    pub title: String,  
    pub app\_id: String,  
    pub workspace\_id: Option\<u64\>,  
    pub is\_focused: bool,  
}
```

This struct is instantiated by parsing JSON payloads received from Niri's IPC interface1:

> * The function parse\_window(v: \&Value) \-\> Option\<NiriWindow\> deserializes a JSON object into a NiriWindow struct1. It extracts the window identifier id using v.get("id")?.as\_u64()?1. String attributes (title, app\_id) are extracted via .and\_then(|t| t.as\_str()) with fallback defaults ("") to prevent runtime panics on missing fields1. Optional numeric workspace identifiers (workspace\_id) and boolean focus flags (is\_focused) are extracted safely1.  
> * The utility function windows\_sorted(map: \&HashMap\<u64, NiriWindow\>) \-\> Vec\<NiriWindow\> converts an unordered hash map of windows into a sorted vector1. Ordering is determined first by workspace\_id (defaulting unassigned windows to 0), and secondarily by numeric window id1.  
> * The function get\_niri\_windows\_map() \-\> HashMap\<u64, NiriWindow\> executes niri msg \-j windows as a synchronous child process1. If process execution fails or yields a non-zero exit status, it returns an empty map1. Upon success, standard output is parsed using serde\_json::from\_str::\<Value\> and transformed into a lookup map indexed by window id1.

### **Niri IPC Communication and Interpolated Window Motion**

Window focusing and movement operations rely on CLI process invocations and native Unix socket connections1:

> * The helper function focus\_window(id: u64) executes niri msg action focus-window \--id \<id\> asynchronously using Command::spawn()1.  
> * The function get\_focused\_window\_id() \-\> Option\<u64\> queries niri msg \-j focused-window, parsing standard output to extract the focused window id1.  
> * The function get\_window\_position(id: u64) \-\> Option\<(f64, f64, bool)\> establishes a Unix domain socket connection to Niri using niri\_ipc::socket::Socket::connect()1. It transmits Request::Windows and pattern-matches the response Response::Windows(windows)1. Upon locating the matching window id, it extracts the workspace tile coordinates ![][image3] from layout.tile\_pos\_in\_workspace\_view along with the is\_floating boolean flag1.  
> * The helper send\_action(action: Action) connects to the Niri socket and fires an action request (Request::Action(action)), ignoring connection failures1.

The nudge\_window function executes a cubic ease-out displacement animation on floating windows1:

```Rust  
fn nudge\_window(id: u64, offset\_y: f64, on\_done: impl Fn() \+ 'static)
```

The algorithm queries window geometry via get\_window\_position(id)1. If the window is missing or tiled (\!is\_floating), execution invokes on\_done() and exits immediately1. For floating windows, step counts are initialized (OUT\_STEPS \= 5, BACK\_STEPS \= 5\) alongside tick intervals (TICK\_MS \= 16, approximating a ![][image4] execution cadence)1. A shared step counter step \= Rc::new(Cell::new(0u32)) tracks animation progress1.  
Inside a glib::timeout\_add\_local closure1:

> 1. If the step counter ![][image5] (![][image6] steps), the window position is explicitly restored to its original baseline ![][image3] via Action::MoveFloatingWindow, on\_done() is executed, and glib::ControlFlow::Break terminates the GLib timer1.  
> 2. For outward steps ![][image7], normalized progress ![][image8] is transformed through a cubic ease-out function:  
>    ![][image9]  
>    The interpolated Y-coordinate is calculated as:  
>    ![][image10]  
> 3. For return steps ![][image11], normalized progress ![][image12] is smoothed through the cubic curve to compute displacement back from ![][image13] to ![][image14]1.  
> 4. The helper send\_action dispatches updated spatial coordinates to Niri, the step counter increments, and glib::ControlFlow::Continue maintains timer iteration1.

The orchestration function focus\_window\_animated(id: u64) coordinates window movement1. It queries the current focused window ID1. If no window is focused or if the target window is already focused, it calls focus\_window(id) directly1. Otherwise, it nudges the previously focused window downward by ![][image15] while simultaneously nudging the target window upward by ![][image16], focusing the target window upon animation completion1.  
The function preview\_window(...) manages temporary hover focusing1. On pointer enter, it records the active window ID, temporarily focuses the hovered window, and hooks an EventControllerMotion::connect\_leave signal listener1. When the mouse pointer leaves the dock button, the leave listener restores focus to the original window unless a click gesture was committed (committed.get() \== true)1.

### **Event Stream Monitoring Daemon**

The function spawn\_niri\_watcher() \-\> std::sync::mpsc::Receiver\<Vec\<NiriWindow\>\> spawns an OS thread running an event stream loop1. It populates an initial window map via get\_niri\_windows\_map() and transmits the sorted list through an MPSC channel1.  
Inside an infinite loop, it spawns niri msg \-j event-stream with stdout piped1. A BufReader parses incoming JSON lines1:

> * WindowsChanged: Clears internal maps and re-populates all window objects1.  
> * WindowOpenedOrChanged: Inserts or updates specific window records1.  
> * WindowClosed: Removes the specified window ID from internal storage1.  
> * WindowFocusChanged: Updates is\_focused booleans across all stored map entries1.

If any event mutates state (changed \== true), the updated window list is sorted via windows\_sorted and sent over the channel1. If the event stream process terminates, the thread sleeps for ![][image17], re-queries the window map, and re-establishes the stream process1.

### **GTK4 Dock UI Construction and Lifecycle**

The constructor make\_dock\_button(win: \&NiriWindow) \-\> Button generates individual dock buttons1:

> * Resolves icon names from win.app\_id (falling back to "application-x-executable") and sets fixed pixel size (![][image18])1.  
> * Sets tooltip text to win.title or win.app\_id1.  
> * Applies CSS classes dockBtn and conditionally dockBtnActive if win.is\_focused is true1.  
> * Attaches a GestureClick controller setting committed \= true on press1.  
> * Connects connect\_clicked signals to cancel pending hover timers, disconnect motion handlers, and trigger focus\_window\_animated(id)1.  
> * Attaches EventControllerMotion: connect\_enter starts a ![][image19] GLib timeout1. If the pointer remains hovering when the timer fires, preview\_window executes1. connect\_leave cancels pending timers1.

The function update\_dockbox(dockbox: \&GtkBox, state: \&Rc\<RefCell\<DockState\>\>, windows: &\[NiriWindow\]) updates the dock layout1:

> * Extracts window IDs into new\_order1.  
> * If new\_order matches state.order, it avoids re-creating widgets1. Instead, it updates CSS focus classes and tooltips in-place across existing buttons1.  
> * If ordering changes, it clears all GTK child widgets from dockbox, resets stored button references, and rebuilds dock buttons sequentially1. If windows is empty, it renders a placeholder dockEmpty label ("No open apps")1.

The constructor spawn\_altdock(app: \&Application, dockbox: GtkBox) \-\> ApplicationWindow initializes the dock surface1:

> * Instantiates an ApplicationWindow assigned CSS class dockOverlay1.  
> * Configures Layer Shell: Layer::Top, Edge::Top anchor set to true, transparent background class removed1.  
> * Spawns the Niri watcher thread and configures a ![][image20] GLib local timeout loop to drain channel receivers, invoking update\_dockbox whenever new window states arrive1.  
> * Attaches motion controllers to dockbox to animate entry and exit overlay classes (dockcum on enter, dockleave on leave) with ![][image17] and ![][image21] timeout delays before hiding the surface1.

## **Chapter 2: Architectural Analysis of ctrl.rs**

The ctrl.rs module provides a control center overlay displaying user identity, network connectivity states, Wi-Fi access point discovery list containers, audio volume sliders, and quick toggle buttons3.

### **Subsystem State Representations**

State structures represent system status3:

```Rust  
\#\[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)\]  
pub enum NetworkState {  
    WifiConnected(String),         
    EthernetConnected(String),     
    NoInternet,                   
    Disconnected,  
    WifiOff,  
}

\#\[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)\]  
pub struct SoundState {  
    pub volume:  u32,  
    pub muted:   bool,  
    pub sink:    String,  
}
```

### **Audio Probing and Monitoring**

Audio state evaluation uses shell process invocations3:

> * The function get\_sound\_state() \-\> SoundState executes wpctl get-volume @DEFAULT\_AUDIO\_SINK@3. It parses standard output for "\[MUTED\]" status and floating-point volume levels (e.g., 0.50), converting raw values via (v \* 100.0).round() as u323.  
> * Queries active sink names using pactl get-default-sink3. Standard output from pactl list sinks is parsed to match Name: against default sink names, extracting human-readable Description: strings3.  
> * The helper sound\_icon(state: \&SoundState) \-\> &'static str maps audio states to icon file paths3: muted or ![][image22] maps to soundmute.svg, ![][image23] to soundlow.svg, ![][image24] to soundmed.svg, and ![][image25] to soundhigh.svg3.  
> * The function spawn\_sound\_watcher(interval: Duration) \-\> Receiver\<SoundState\> spawns a thread polling get\_sound\_state() on interval ticks, emitting updates over an MPSC channel when SoundState mutates3.

### **Network Interface and Connectivity Diagnostics**

Network inspection reads kernel sysfs interfaces directly3:

> * The utility wifi\_soft\_blocked() \-\> bool iterates /sys/class/rfkill/\* entries3. It reads type (checking for "wlan") and soft (checking for "1"), returning true if Wi-Fi is soft-blocked3.  
> * The diagnostic function has\_internet() \-\> bool inspects /proc/net/route for default gateway entries matching destination 000000003. If present, it attempts a TCP stream socket connection to 1.1.1.1:53 with a 2-second timeout3.  
> * The helper wifi\_ssid(iface: \&str) \-\> Option\<String\> executes lookup tools:  
  1. Executes nmcli \-t \-f ACTIVE,SSID dev wifi, matching lines starting with yes:3.  
  2. Executes iw dev \<iface\> link, stripping SSID: prefixes3.  
  3. Executes iwgetid \<iface\> \-r as fallback3.  
> * The function get\_network\_state() \-\> NetworkState inspects /sys/class/net/\* network interfaces3. Skips loopback ("lo")3. Reads operstate ("up" vs "down") and checks for presence of /sys/class/net/\<iface\>/wireless directories3.  
  * If wireless exists, interfaces are up, but soft-blocked, returns NetworkState::WifiOff3.  
  * If no interfaces are connected, returns NetworkState::Disconnected3.  
  * If connected but TCP probe fails, returns NetworkState::NoInternet3.  
  * Returns NetworkState::WifiConnected(ssid) or NetworkState::EthernetConnected(iface) accordingly3.  
> * The function spawn\_network\_watcher(interval: Duration) polls network state on interval ticks, sending updates over an MPSC channel on change3.  
> * The helper toggle\_wifi\_adapter(enable: bool) executes rfkill unblock wifi or rfkill block wifi3.  
> * The function get\_wifi\_networks() \-\> Vec\<(String, String, bool)\> executes nmcli \-t \-f ACTIVE,SSID,SIGNAL,SECURITY dev wifi list3. Parses colon-delimited standard output into active status, SSID, and signal bars derived from signal percentage:  
  * ![][image26]  
  * ![][image27]  
  * ![][image28]  
  * ![][image29]

Returns a list sorted with connected networks first3.

### **Control Capsule UI Assembly and Rendering**

The function spawn\_ctrl\_capsules(app: \&Application, overlay\_open: Rc\<RefCell\<bool\>\>) \-\> ApplicationWindow builds the control panel surface3:

> * Layer shell configuration: Layer::Top, full-screen anchors (Top, Bottom, Left, Right set to true), transparent backdrop buttons3.

Avatar rendering resolves file paths matching /usr/share/octobacillus/usericon.\* (png, jpeg, jpg)3. It loads a Pixbuf and instantiates a ![][image30] DrawingArea3.  
The set\_draw\_func closure renders a custom circular user avatar using Cairo3:

> 1. Clips rendering context to a circle: cr.arc(cx, cy, r, 0.0, 2.0 \* PI) and cr.clip()3.  
> 2. Scales Pixbuf using bilinear interpolation (InterpType::Bilinear) and paints it3.  
> 3. Constructs a diagonal linear gradient shine (LinearGradient::new):  
   * Color stop ![][image31]  
   * Color stop ![][image32]  
   * Color stop ![][image33]  
> 4. Applies transform matrix scaling (![][image34]) and fills an elliptical highlight arc3.  
> 5. Draws an outer rim stroke (![][image35] width) using a linear gradient along the arc ![][image36]3.

The interface reads username strings from /usr/share/octobacillus/user.octo parsing name \= \<val\> lines3. It builds a network status button (netbtn), an expandable Wi-Fi drawer (net\_panel) containing adapter switch toggles, network rescan buttons (nmcli dev wifi rescan), settings buttons (nmcli-connection-editor), and GTK ListBox containers displaying available networks3. Scroll controllers attached to sound buttons (soundbtn) intercept vertical scroll events to execute wpctl set-volume \-l 1.0 @DEFAULT\_AUDIO\_SINK@ 5%+ or 5%-, scheduling ![][image37] GLib timeouts to update volume labels3.

## **Chapter 3: Architectural Analysis of main.rs**

The main.rs file serves as the main entry point2. It handles workspace toggling, drag-and-drop file/URL handling (clippy), status bar displays, probe config parsing, and dynamic widget lifecycles2.

### **Probe Configuration Parser and State Polling**

The system reads configuration parameters from /var/lib/cynager/info.probe2:

```Rust  
\#\[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)\]  
struct WidgetConfig {  
    cal:      bool,  
    sys:      bool,  
    shellout: String,  
    bat:      bool,  
    stick:    bool,  
}
```

The function parse\_widget\_config(path: \&str) \-\> Option\<WidgetConfig\> parses probe files using text markers2:

> 1. Locates :set block boundaries2.  
> 2. Scans for shellout : \<value\> to extract monitor output strings2.  
> 3. Locates widgets { ... } block boundaries2.  
> 4. Parses lines stripping leading : and splitting key-value pairs separated by : (e.g., cal:true, sys:false)2.

The watcher spawn\_probe\_watcher(probe\_path: String, interval: Duration) executes a polling thread reading configuration states and emitting updates across an MPSC channel whenever configuration changes2.

### **Monitor Connector Resolution and Surface Binding**

The helper resolve\_monitor(display: \&Display, connector: \&str) \-\> Option\<Monitor\> iterates active monitors in GDK display contexts2. Matches monitor.connector() against configuration strings (e.g., "eDP-1"), returning matching Monitor references2. The helper pin\_to\_monitor(window: \&ApplicationWindow, monitor: Option\<\&Monitor\>) anchors layer shell surfaces to target monitors2.

### **Window Layout Records and Corner Hiding Interpolation**

To support workspace toggling, main.rs manages window state records2:

```Rust  
\#\[derive(Clone)\]  
struct WindowRecord {  
    id:           u64,  
    workspace\_id: Option\<u64\>,  
    column\_index: Option\<usize\>,  
    row\_index:    Option\<usize\>,  
    is\_floating:  bool,  
    float\_x:      Option\<f64\>,  
    float\_y:      Option\<f64\>,  
    float\_w:      i32,  
    float\_h:      i32,  
    corner\_x:     Option\<f64\>,  
    corner\_y:     Option\<f64\>,  
}
```

> * The function get\_windows() \-\> Vec\<WindowRecord\> queries the Niri socket using Request::Windows2. Maps tiling column/row indices from layout.pos\_in\_scrolling\_layout and tile coordinates from layout.tile\_pos\_in\_workspace\_view2.  
> * The utility get\_focused\_output\_size() \-\> Option\<(f64, f64)\> queries Request::FocusedOutput returning screen resolution ![][image38]2.  
> * The helper corner\_hide\_target(...) computes target offscreen coordinates for floating windows while maintaining a ![][image39] visible peek edge (PEEK \= 10.0)2:  
  * Determines center coordinates:  
    ![][image40]  
  * Target ![][image41]: if ![][image42], sets ![][image43]; else ![][image44]2.  
  * Target ![][image45]: if ![][image46], sets ![][image47]; else ![][image48]2.  
> * The function animate\_float\_window(...) runs a 12-step cubic ease-out animation (![][image1] ticks) updating floating window positions via Action::MoveFloatingWindow2.

### **Battery Diagnostics and Polling**

The function get\_battery\_state() \-\> Option\<BatteryState\> inspects /sys/class/power\_supply/BAT\* or CMB\*2. Reads capacity percentage and status ("Charging" vs "Discharging")2. If capacity drops below ![][image49] while discharging and /tmp/batt\_no\_ask.var is absent, it spawns the low battery warning process batt\_low2. The helper battery\_icon maps charge ranges (![][image50], ![][image51], ![][image52], ![][image53]) and charging flags to SVG icon paths2.

### **Drag-and-Drop Clipboard Target (Clippy)**

Inside coping\_with, the clippy widget provides a drag-and-drop collector target2:

> * Instantiates DropTarget accepting gio::File and string types with actions COPY | MOVE2.  
> * The function add\_file\_to\_clippy: Resolves URI types (file://), decodes percent-encoded characters via percent\_decode, maps icons via icon\_for\_path, and resolves MIME types via mime\_for\_path2.  
> * Constructs GTK buttons displaying file icons2. Attaches GTK DragSource providers supplying text/uri-list, GFile handles, and binary file byte streams2. Right-click (GestureClick button 3\) removes items from clipboard containers2.  
> * The function add\_text\_to\_clippy: Truncates text previews to 40 characters, constructs label buttons, configures clipboard writes on left-click (display.clipboard().set\_text(...)), and attaches DragSource supplying text/plain content2.  
> * The function add\_link\_to\_clippy: Generates web link buttons using icon emblem-web supplying text/uri-list and plain text content for dragging2.

### **Shell Orchestration and Signal Registration**

The entry routine coping\_with(app: \&Application) coordinates shell startup2:

> 1. Initializes notification daemon channel receivers2.  
> 2. Loads CSS styling from \~/.config/capsule/dark.css2.  
> 3. Resolves monitor bindings and creates layer shell windows: TimeCapsule top bar, capsuleO OSD window, and capsuleN notification panel2.  
> 4. Instantiates probe config watcher threads, dynamically spawning or terminating desktop widgets (spawn\_calendar\_widget, spawn\_sys\_widget, spawn\_stick\_widget, spawn\_bat\_widget) via kill() helpers2.  
> 5. Registers UNIX signal listener SIGUSR1 via glib::unix\_signal\_add\_local2:  
   * **Hide State (is\_hidden \== false)**: Captures window topology via get\_windows(), records current focused window, sets is\_hidden \= true, and animates floating windows to corner target coordinates2.  
   * **Unhide State (is\_hidden \== true)**: Restores recorded windows to original workspaces via Action::MoveWindowToWorkspace2. Sorts tiled windows by column and row index, focusing columns and issuing Action::ConsumeWindowIntoColumn and Action::MoveWindowUp to reconstruct tiled column layouts2. Animates floating windows back to original coordinates and re-focuses initial window IDs2.  
> 6. Spawns server-side window decorations via ssd::spawn\_shelly\_side\_decorations(app)2.

The main function instantiates GTK Application ekah.scu.cynideshell, binds activate to coping\_with, and enters execution loops2.

## **Chapter 4: Architectural Analysis of notifications.rs**

The notifications.rs module implements a freedesktop-compliant notification daemon4. It hosts a DBus session bus service using zbus, handles audio chime playback via rodio, and animates status bar expansion popups4.

### **DBus Interface Mapping and Registration**

Notification structures model payload data4:

```Rust  
\#\[derive(Debug, Clone)\]  
pub struct Notification {  
    pub id: u32,  
    pub app\_name: String,  
    pub summary: String,  
    pub body: String,  
    pub icon: String,  
    pub \_timestamp: std::time::Instant,  
    pub \_actions: Vec\<String\>  
}
```

The DBus interface structure exports methods4:

```Rust  
struct NotificationServer {  
    sender: mpsc::UnboundedSender\<Notification\>,  
    next\_id: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32,  
}
```

\#\[zbus::interface(name \= "org.freedesktop.Notifications")\]  
impl NotificationServer { ... }

> * Method notify(...): Asynchronous DBus method invoked by external applications4.  
  * Increments atomic counter next\_id using Ordering::Relaxed4.  
  * Resolves notification icon strings: prioritizes explicit app\_icon, falls back to hints keys ("image-path", "app-icon"), or defaults to lowercase app\_name4.  
  * Constructs Notification structs and transmits them across Tokio unbounded MPSC channel sender4.  
  * Returns allocated notification id4.  
> * Method get\_capabilities(): Returns vector \["body", "persistence"\]4.  
> * Method get\_server\_information(): Returns server metadata tuple ("capsule", "ekah", "1.0", "1.2")4.

The function spawn\_messaging\_daemon() \-\> UnboundedReceiver\<Notification\> spawns an OS thread running a Tokio async runtime4. The runtime establishes a DBus session bus connection, registers NotificationServer under service name org.freedesktop.Notifications at path /org/freedesktop/Notifications, and blocks asynchronously4.

### **Audio Chime Playback Engine**

The function play\_notification\_sound() checks notification sound preferences4:

> * Reads /var/lib/cynager/info.probe, parsing :set blocks for key dnd4.  
> * If dnd is "false", spawns a thread initializing rodio::OutputStream and Sink4.  
> * Opens sound file /var/lib/cynager/niri/sound/notiv/notiv.mp3, decodes audio via rodio::Decoder, and streams playback through sound output sinks4.

### **Notification Center and Status Bar Animation Logic**

The connection routine connect\_notifications\_to\_dock(...) hooks notification channels into GTK main loops4:

> * Spawns GTK local async tasks ctx.spawn\_local consuming incoming notifications4.  
> * Stores notification items in a bounded ring buffer history (VecDeque capped at 50 entries)4.  
> * Resolves icon presence in system icon themes via Gdk::IconTheme::has\_icon4. Updates status bar icons (app\_img), triggers CSS spinning coin animations (spinning-coin), updates badge labels, and triggers play\_notification\_sound()4.  
> * Evaluates incoming notifications against last\_group state4. If summary matches previous summary, appends text labels to existing popover container rather than duplicating root entries4.  
> * On new notifications, constructs horizontal notificationAll box containers4:  
  * Displays application icons, summary text, truncated body labels, and app names4.  
  * Attaches GTK Popover containing full wrapped body text4.  
  * Attaches hover controllers (EventControllerMotion): entering pointer triggers ![][image17] timers showing popovers (pop.popup()) with CSS animation class popupanim4. Exiting pointer hides popovers4.  
  * Constructs single item close buttons (deleteBtn) and clear-all buttons (clearBtn) with vanish animation transitions4.

When a notification arrives, status bar width expands4:

> 1. Obtains monitor display dimensions, deriving target expanded width:  
>    ![][image54]  
> 2. Defines baseline width ![][image55]4.  
> 3. Computes linear interpolation step size per frame (![][image56] interval):  
>    ![][image57]  
> 4. Executes frame-by-frame timer loops incrementing current width ![][image58], invoking noti\_window.set\_width\_request(W\_cur) until target width is reached, then applies CSS class blip4.  
> 5. Elevates top bar surface layer to Layer::Overlay4.  
> 6. Schedules a 10-second auto-dismiss GLib timeout4. When pending notifications decay to zero, resets badge labels, removes animation CSS classes, runs interpolation loops in reverse decreasing width back to ![][image59], and restores surface layer to Layer::Top4.

## **Chapter 5: Architectural Analysis of osd.rs**

The osd.rs module renders On-Screen Display (OSD) feedback popups when system volume, microphone mute state, or display brightness changes5.

### **Event Model and Execution Wrappers**

Hardware feedback events are typed5:

```Rust  
\#\[derive(Debug, Clone)\]  
pub enum OsdEvent {  
    Volume     { volume: u32, muted: bool },  
    Mute       { muted: bool, volume: u32 },  
    MicMute    { muted: bool },  
    MicInUse   { active: bool },  
    Brightness { percent: u32 },  
}
```

Hardware adjustment utilities execute CLI commands5:

> * The helper adjust\_volume(delta: f64) dispatches pactl set-sink-volume @DEFAULT\_SINK@ \+5% or \-5%5.  
> * The helper adjust\_brightness(delta: f64) dispatches brightnessctl set \+5% or 5%-5.

### **Sysfs Inotify Backlight Monitor**

Display brightness changes are monitored via kernel sysfs events5:

> * The utility find\_backlight() \-\> Option\<(PathBuf, u64)\> scans /sys/class/backlight/\*5. Verifies existence of brightness and max\_brightness sysfs nodes, parsing maximum brightness values5.  
> * The function read\_brightness\_percent(path, max) \-\> Option\<u32\> reads current brightness integers, calculating percentages:  
>   ![][image60]  
> * The watcher spawn\_brightness\_watcher() \-\> Option\<Receiver\<u32\>\> spawns an OS thread initializing Linux inotify on brightness sysfs paths5. Monitors WatchMask::CLOSE\_WRITE | WatchMask::MODIFY flags5. On file write events, reads updated percentage values and emits changes over an MPSC channel5.  
> * The function connect\_brightness(...) hooks channels into GLib event loops using ![][image61] periodic timeouts, invoking show\_osd() upon receiving brightness updates5.

### **Native PulseAudio GLib Asynchronous Event Loop**

The entry routine connect\_osd\_to\_dock(...) integrates with PulseAudio using C-bindings (libpulse\_binding, libpulse\_glib\_binding)5:

> * Creates an invisible ![][image62] scroll pad (scrollPad) attached to capsule surfaces5. Binds vertical scroll events to adjust\_volume or adjust\_brightness based on active modes5.  
> * Initializes PulseAudio GLib main loop wrappers Mainloop::new(None) and context Context::new(&\*ml, "capsule-osd")5.  
> * Configures context state callbacks5. When context state switches to ContextState::Ready, schedules on\_context\_ready() via glib::idle\_add\_local\_once5.  
> * Calls context.connect(None, ContextFlagSet::NOFLAGS, None) establishing asynchronous IPC connections5.

Inside on\_context\_ready:

> 1. Triggers initial introspection queries: fetch\_sink\_info and fetch\_source\_info5.  
> 2. Subscribes to PulseAudio facility events: context.subscribe(InterestMaskSet::SINK | InterestMaskSet::SOURCE)5.  
> 3. Configures subscription callbacks matching facility changes (Facility::Sink or Facility::Source with SubOp::Changed), triggering re-introspection queries5.

The function fetch\_sink\_info introspects default audio sink @DEFAULT\_SINK@5:

> * Converts raw PulseAudio volume info.volume.avg() to percentages using pa\_vol\_to\_percent:  
>   ![][image63]  
> * Updates thread-local AudioState5. If volume or muted state changes, fires show\_osd() with OsdEvent::Volume or OsdEvent::Mute payloads5.

The function fetch\_source\_info introspects default audio source @DEFAULT\_SOURCE@5:

> * Evaluates source mute status info.mute and running state SourceState::Running5.  
> * Fires show\_osd() with OsdEvent::MicMute or OsdEvent::MicInUse payloads when microphone properties change5.

### **OSD Rendering and Auto-Hide Timer Controls**

The display routine show\_osd(...) manages OSD surface display and auto-hide timing5:

> 1. Dispatches apply\_osd\_event(): resets CSS classes (osd-volume, osd-muted, osd-mic, osd-brightness), clears previous label text, calculates filled bar width (![][image64]), applies progress styling, and sets text labels5.  
> 2. If OSD surface is not currently visible, calls window.present(), reveals the revealer child, and applies reveal animation CSS class osd-show5.  
> 3. Clears any existing GLib hide timeout source ID5.  
> 4. Schedules a new 3-second GLib timeout (timeout\_add\_seconds\_local(3))5. When the timer fires, applies hide animation CSS class osd-hide, schedules a ![][image65] timer to set revealer child to hidden (set\_reveal\_child(false)), hides the GTK window surface, and clears source ID handles5.

## **Chapter 6: Architectural Analysis of ssd.rs**

The ssd.rs module renders server-side window decorations (close, minimize, and float/fullscreen controls) positioned over active Niri windows6.

### **Geometry Structures and Event Channels**

Data structures capture geometry6:

```Rust  
\#\[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)\]  
struct FocusedGeo {  
    x: i32,  
    y: i32,  
    xsize: i32,  
    ysize: i32,  
    output: String,  
    is\_floating: bool,  
}

\#\[derive(Debug)\]  
enum SsdEvent {  
    Focused(FocusedGeo),  
    NoFocus,  
}
```

### **Window Decoration Controls and Key Synthesis**

The routine spawn\_shelly\_side\_decorations(app: \&gtk4::Application) constructs decoration surface windows6:

> * Instantiates ApplicationWindow titled "capsuleSSD", anchored to Layer Shell Layer::Overlay, anchored Top and Left, with keyboard mode set to KeyboardMode::None6.  
> * Constructs button bar (ssdBar) holding controls6:  
  * Control btn\_close: connect\_clicked dispatches Niri action CloseWindow6.  
  * Control btn\_float: connect\_clicked dispatches Niri action FullscreenWindow6.  
  * Control btn\_min: Toggles Super key holding state6. Executes shell utility ydotool key \--key-delay=0 125:1 (press Super) or 125:0 (release Super), updating active CSS styling (ssdMinActive)6.  
> * Registers UNIX signal handler SIGUSR2 via glib::unix\_signal\_add\_local6. Releases Super key state (ydotool key ... 125:0) and removes active CSS styling6.  
> * Includes date and time labels (ampm) updated every ![][image66] via GLib timeouts6.

### **Event Stream Consumer Thread**

The thread loop niri\_event\_loop(tx: mpsc::Sender\<SsdEvent\>) runs continuous event monitoring loops6:

> 1. Transmits initial focus geometry states via query\_focused\_geo()6.  
> 2. Connects to Niri Unix sockets (Socket::connect()) and transmits Request::EventStream6.  
> 3. Enters continuous blocking event loops reading stream events6. On receiving stream messages, re-queries focused window geometry via query\_focused\_geo() and transmits updated SsdEvent instances over channels6.

The query function query\_focused\_geo() \-\> Option\<FocusedGeo\> inspects compositor state6:

> * Transmits Request::Workspaces to retrieve active workspace outputs6.  
> * Transmits Request::FocusedWindow to extract focused window properties6.  
> * Extracts tile coordinates ![][image3] from layout.tile\_pos\_in\_workspace\_view, tile dimensions ![][image67] from layout.tile\_size, workspace output connector names, and is\_floating boolean flags6. Returns populated FocusedGeo structs6.

### **Geometry Tracking Execution Loop**

In the main GTK thread, spawn\_shelly\_side\_decorations schedules a ![][image1] (![][image2]) GLib local timeout loop to align decoration overlays with focused window coordinates6:

> 1. Drains MPSC channel receiver rx, capturing the latest SsdEvent6.  
> 2. On SsdEvent::Focused(geo):  
   * **Monitor Alignment**: Checks if target output connector (geo.output) matches current monitor bindings6. If changed, looks up monitors via find\_monitor\_by\_connector and anchors window surfaces to target monitors via win.set\_monitor6.  
   * **Floating Window Positioning**: Sets margins set\_margin(Edge::Top, geo.y \+ 7\) and set\_margin(Edge::Left, geo.x \+ 7), positions overlays directly over window top edges, detaches top bar time displays, and reveals window surfaces6.  
   * **Tiled Window Positioning**: Hides window surfaces, attaches top bar time displays, anchors right edges (Edge::Right), and updates margins to match tiling layout bounds6.  
> 3. On SsdEvent::NoFocus: Hides decoration surfaces6.

## **Inter-Subsystem Event Flow and Socket Protocol Reference**

The table below catalogs system events, Unix signal handlers, socket IPC methods, and internal triggers dispatches across the CynageOS suite.

| Trigger Source | Event Identifier / Signal | Target Subsystem Callback | Prerequisite State | Resulting UI & System State Action |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| External OS Signal | SIGUSR1 | main.rs (unix\_signal\_add\_local)2. | Desktop active2. | Toggles workspace hidden mode; animates floating windows offscreen or restores window column topology2. |
| External OS Signal | SIGUSR2 | ssd.rs (unix\_signal\_add\_local)6. | Super key held active6. | Forces synthetic key release via ydotool and clears minimize button active CSS classes6. |
| Niri Socket Stream | WindowsChanged | altdock.rs (spawn\_niri\_watcher)1. | Windows created/destroyed1. | Re-queries window topology, re-sorts array, and updates dock button containers1. |
| Niri Socket Stream | WindowFocusChanged | altdock.rs & ssd.rs event streams1. | Focus switched between windows1. | Updates active dock CSS highlight; repositions server-side decorations to new window boundaries1. |
| DBus Session Bus | notify Method | notifications.rs (NotificationServer)4. | External notification sent4. | Allocates ID, plays chime via rodio, constructs popover rows, and animates top bar width expansion4. |
| Linux Inotify | MODIFY / CLOSE\_WRITE | osd.rs (spawn\_brightness\_watcher)5. | Sysfs brightness node written5. | Calculates brightness percentage and presents OSD overlay with auto-hide timer5. |
| PulseAudio Socket | Facility::Sink / Source | osd.rs (on\_context\_ready)5. | Volume changed or mic muted5. | Re-introspects audio state and reveals volume/mic OSD popups5. |
| Linux Sysfs | Power Supply State | main.rs (spawn\_battery\_watcher)2. | Battery status polled (10s interval)2. | Updates status bar tooltip/icon; triggers batt\_low binary if battery ![][image68] while discharging2. |

## **Architectural Synthesis**

The CynageOS shell ecosystem demonstrates an asynchronous desktop architecture built on GTK4 and Wayland layer shell interfaces1. By isolating hardware monitoring threads, DBus communication channels, and IPC event streams from the GTK main event loop, the system executes real-time cubic easing animations, dynamic spatial layout tracking, and overlay transitions without blocking rendering execution1. The modular design ensures component isolation, allowing individual desktop components (including application docks, control capsules, OSD feedback windows, and server-side window decorations) to operate as responsive user interface overlays alongside the Niri scrollable-tiling compositor1.
